integrity: The proof is analytic. It uses the exact disjoint-support three-halves Lebesgue norm, Hölder and Sobolev inequalities, and standard essential-spectrum stability for finite compactly supported Schrödinger perturbations. No numerical experiment is used as proof.
scientific_limitations: The coupling bound is sufficient rather than sharp; the result concerns the three-dimensional regular-well model and does not settle the binding-regime optimization problem. At the endpoint the argument proves nonnegativity but does not exclude a zero-energy resonance. If the conjectural phrase principal eigenvalue was intended to restrict the domain to already-binding configurations, the result supplies a necessary explicit binding hypothesis rather than a contradiction to that restricted reading.
title: Weak-coupling nonuniqueness in three-dimensional quantum-dot loop optimization
